generation.explanation: The line of best fit (least-squares regression line) is the line ŷ = mx + b that makes the sum of squared vertical distances from the points to the line as small as possible. The slope is m = Σ(x−x̄)(y−ȳ) / Σ(x−x̄)², and the line always passes through the mean point (x̄, ȳ). Drag any yellow point and the line, the equation, and R² (how much of the variation in y the line explains) all update right away. Turn on residuals to see the vertical red gaps the line is minimizing. A single outlier can pull the line a long way.
